automation_evidence.finding: Ambient AI scribe pilot at Stanford Health Care: 48 physicians over 3 months; paired survey (n=38) showed task load fell 24.42 points and burnout fell 1.94 points (both p<.001), usability rose 10.9 (p<.001). Pre-post quality-improvement design with no control arm and single institution.

Systematic review of 11 AI-scribe implementation studies (10 published 2024): 9 of 10 studies reporting an efficiency metric showed improvement and 7 of 10 showed positive effects on clinician wellness/burnout, but scribe accuracy varied and frequently required manual edits, with occasional error concerns.

Cluster-randomized crossover trial, 22 dentists x 20 bitewings: AI caries support raised mean AUC from 0.85 to 0.89 and sensitivity from 0.72 to 0.81 (p<.05) with no significant specificity change, but AI use also increased invasive treatment decisions - a clinical-risk side effect of automation.

Meta-analysis of 21 controlled studies on approximal caries detection from bitewings: pooled AI sensitivity 0.94 and specificity 0.91, but positive predictive value ranged only 0.15-0.87 while negative predictive value was 0.79-1.00. AI is reliable for ruling out healthy surfaces, not for confirming disease without expert review.

Meta-analysis of 14 studies on AI caries detection/classification from bitewings: diagnostic odds ratio 55.8 (95% CI 28.8-108.3), summary sensitivity 0.87 and specificity 0.89, yet most included studies had unclear or high risk of bias and few were externally validated; dataset sizes 112-3,686 radiographs.

Lifetime Markov cost-effectiveness modelling of AI decision support in dentistry (US/Germany/Brazil cohorts): AI cost about EUR 320 vs EUR 342 for standard care and produced 62.4 vs 60.9 tooth-retention years - statistically marginal, with conclusions sensitive to the fee paid for AI and to the treatment chosen after diagnosis.

Rapid systematic review of predictive-model-based no-show interventions (7 RCTs + 1 non-RCT): model-driven text reminders reduced no-shows (1 RCT, median RR 0.91, high certainty), phone-call reminders median RR 0.61 across 3 RCTs (moderate certainty), and patient navigators RR 0.55 (95% CI 0.46-0.67). Cost-effectiveness, acceptability and equity were rarely reported.

Pilot RCT with 720 pediatric/family-medicine patients who had no-showed: up to three text messages raised completed rescheduled visits by 2.83 percentage points (95% CI 1.66-4.00; OR 1.86), while the effect on merely rescheduling was not statistically significant. Small effect, one health system.

RCT (170 patients) in an urban pediatric resident clinic: adding a text-message reminder to the standard voice reminder cut no-show rate from 38.1% to 23.5% (14.6 pp difference, p=0.04). Small single-site study from 2014-15 data.

common_tools: Practice-management / scheduling-and-billing systems used as the system of record in dental offices, PT clinics and veterinary hospitals (O*NET lists scheduling, billing, insurance-form and record-keeping as embedded tasks for 31-9091 and 29-2056)

Radiology and imaging systems: dental assistants expose diagnostic x-rays and vet technicians take diagnostic radiographs, so imaging is the attachment point for AI caries/radiograph tools (O*NET 31-9091, 29-2056)

HIPAA standard electronic transactions and code sets - CMS specifies national standards for electronic transactions, code sets, unique identifiers and operating rules that any agent generating or consuming claims/eligibility traffic must conform to
Controlled-substance inventory and drug log systems in veterinary practices (O*NET 29-2056: 'maintain controlled drug inventory and related log books')
EHR/EMR clinical documentation and note templates - the target of the ambient AI scribes evaluated in JAMIA (2025) and Appl Clin Inform (2025)
SMS / patient-portal reminder and recall messaging - the delivery channel in the no-show RCTs (JAMIA 2023 review; Acad Pediatr 2024; Int J Pediatr 2016)

Prior-authorization and eligibility/benefit verification workflows (inference: O*NET 31-9091 explicitly includes completing insurance forms and billing, which sit upstream of payer portals; no source verified the specific vendor tooling)
constraints: HIPAA Security Rule compliance: NIST SP 800-66 Rev. 2 is the federal implementation resource guide for the HIPAA Security Rule, which implies vendor business associate agreements, access control, audit logging and encryption for any AI tool touching patient records in dental or PT practices
HIPAA Administrative Simplification requires standard electronic transactions and code sets (CMS), so billing/eligibility agents must emit conforming X12/code-set transactions rather than free text

Scope-of-practice limits are state-set: BLS states each state regulates the scope of practice for dental assistants and that some states require licensing/registration specifically to perform radiography or expanded functions - an agent cannot be authorized to perform duties the assistant is not licensed for

Clinical liability for diagnostic output: pooled positive predictive value for AI caries detection ranged 0.15-0.87, so AI findings cannot be treated as an autonomous diagnosis and must be verified by a licensed clinician

Veterinary controlled-substance recordkeeping is an explicit technician duty (O*NET 29-2056 maintains controlled drug inventory and log books), which makes drug-log automation a regulated record rather than a convenience workflow

PHI is handled at shared front-desk workstations and on personal devices in small practices, which argues for private/BAA-covered or on-premises deployment over consumer-grade cloud AI (inference, based on the front-desk and clerical task set in O*NET 31-9091 and 29-2056)

Multi-site data sensitivity: imaging datasets in the caries studies ranged from 112 to 3,686 radiographs and few models were externally validated, so local (NJ) imaging distributions may differ from vendor training data (inference from the meta-analysis risk-of-bias findings)
trends: BLS projects dental assistant employment to grow 7% from 2025 to 2035 (vs 3% for all occupations), with about 53,000 openings per year nationally, most from replacement rather than growth

BLS projects physical therapist employment to grow 12% from 2025 to 2035, from 283,700 to 317,600 jobs, with about 13,400 openings per year; drivers cited are the aging population, chronic musculoskeletal conditions and non-opioid pain management
BLS projects veterinary technologist/technician employment to grow 9% from 2025 to 2035, with about 13,400 openings per year, and notes 89% work in veterinary services

Retention pressure in veterinary: BLS states veterinary technologists and technicians have one of the highest rates of injuries and illnesses of all occupations (bites, scratches, kicks) and may have to work evenings, weekends or holidays

Labor-cost pressure is higher in NJ than nationally for the same roles - e.g., NJ physical therapist median $50.00/hr (May 2023) and NJ dental assistant median $22.50/hr, against national May 2025 medians of $102,760/yr for PTs and $48,070/yr for dental assistants (inference: NJ hourly medians are relatively high, which shortens payback on task automation)

Low-wage, high-turnover roles persist alongside the licensed roles: NJ physical therapist aides median $14.48/hr and veterinary assistants median $17.82/hr (May 2023), suggesting automation should target coordination and documentation rather than aide labor (inference)
Demand for veterinary services is tied to household pet numbers and pet spending, and BLS expects advances in veterinary medicine plus an aging pet population to drive more complex procedures
caveats: Wage data: the most recent BLS OEWS state tables available as readable HTML for New Jersey are May 2023; BLS has moved May 2024 and May 2025 state and metro tables to an interactive app (data.bls.gov/oes) that could not be read programmatically, so NJ figures are roughly 2 years older than the national OOH figures (May 2025) quoted in trends. No Middlesex County or Edison/New Brunswick metro-division wage cuts were obtained. Automation evidence: the strongest items (cluster RCT, meta-analyses) measure diagnostic accuracy on curated radiograph sets, not time saved, revenue recovered or error rates in a real practice; the AI-scribe evidence is single-institution pre-post or a review of 11 mostly 2024 studies, i.e. early and self-reported. No NJ-specific or small-practice automation measurement was found for any of the three sub-industries. No peer-reviewed evidence was located for veterinary AI scribes or for PT-specific AI documentation time savings. Sources were retrieved from NCBI E-utilities (PubMed records cited by PMID) rather than the PubMed web pages themselves. web_search was unavailable throughout this run (both providers rate-limited), so no vendor landscape, trade-press or association-survey scan was possible; zero vendor claims are included and no product names are asserted as verified. Items explicitly labelled 'inference' are analyst reasoning, not sourced statements.
